item.content:encoded:
Sign up for a Try It! class at 92NY Art Center — one-session, no-pressure workshops designed to help you dip a toe into drawing, painting, or abstract art before diving into the full course.

All supplies are provided. No experience is needed. And if you decide to sign up for a multi-week course afterwards, you’ll get $25 off your registration.

Join 92NY in the studio for an evening of creativity — and see what sparks!

Upcoming Try It! classes 

Try It! Watercolor Painting
Explore the basics of watercolor — washes, layering, blending — and see if it’s a fit for you.
Oct 10

Try It! Enameling
A hands-on introduction to enamel, including kiln firing basics and torch firing.
Oct 15

Try It! Landscape Painting
Work in acrylics and explore color mixing, brushwork, and the beauty of landscapes.
Oct 17

Try It! Abstract Art
Want to explore abstract art but don’t know where to start? This class is a chance to play with color, mark-making, and composition while experimenting with different materials.
Oct 24

Try It! Handbuilding and Wheel
Can’t decide between wheel throwing and handbuilding? Try both! In this class, you’ll get a solid introduction to both techniques.
Nov 2

Try It! Collage
Get a quick introduction to collage in this hands-on workshop focused on experimentation and play.
Nov 7

Try It! Oil Painting
Get a feel for the materials and techniques that make oils so rewarding to work with.
Nov 14

Try It! Printmaking
Get a quick introduction to printmaking in this hands-on workshop designed as a first taste of the process.
Nov 19

Space is limited — sign up now to save your seat!

item.content:encoded:
Spend a Friday evening at the Frick—for free!

Louis Vuitton First Fridays
Friday, October 2
5:30 to 9:00 p.m.

The Frick Collection
1 East 70th Street

Grab your friends and join us this Friday for a FREE evening of art and culture! Enjoy live jazz, drop-in drawing, and drinks and bites in the Garden Court. Plus, experience after-hours access to the galleries, exciting talks, and more.

Please note: Only children ages 10 and older are admitted.

These events are offered on the first Friday of each month (except January). Mark your calendar for upcoming installments: October 2, November 6, and December 4.

All gallery talks during First Fridays will offer free assistive listening devices (ALDs). Live American Sign Language (ASL) interpretation is available upon request; we ask for two weeks’ advance notice, but we will make every effort to accommodate all requests. To make a request or for other questions, please email us at accessibility@frick.org.

TICKETS

Advance registration is closed, but walk-ups are welcome! Learn more at frick.org/firstfridays. Plus, sign up for our newsletter to stay up to date on ticket releases for upcoming installments of Louis Vuitton First Fridays.

We are deeply grateful to Louis Vuitton for sponsoring Louis Vuitton First Fridays from June 2026 through May 2027.

item.title: TUES-THURS, 9/29-10/1: FREE COFFEE, PRETTY IN PINK, ARCHTOBER FEST, AND MORE
item.dc:creator: skintadmin
item.description: tuesday tues: national coffee day deals: score a free drip coffee or cold brew at all coffee project new york locations from 2–4pm (2–2:30pm in long island city); grab a free small or medium hot or iced coffee with any purchase at krispy kreme all day. tues 6pm: page break presents: stage break reading series […]
item.content:encoded:
tuesday

tues: national coffee day deals: score a free drip coffee or cold brew at all coffee project new york locations from 2–4pm (2–2:30pm in long island city); grab a free small or medium hot or iced coffee with any purchase at krispy kreme all day.

tues 6pm: page break presents: stage break reading series with astra house: four astra house books writers take the stage to read original short stories, one page at a time, alternating with audience members picked at random to join them (optional: enter your name to read). everyone gets a zine with the four stories, so you can follow along from your seat. presented by page break, a weekend reading retreat. mcnally jackson books at bklyn studios (downtown brooklyn), $10. >>

tues 6:30pm: pretty in pink x straight white men can’t dance with jon cryer + addie tsai: revisit the john hughes 80s classic pretty in pink (written by hughes and directed by howard deutch) on the big screen, followed by a q+a and book signing with author addie tsai and star jon cryer. journalist rich juzwiak moderates the discussion about the film and tsai’s new book, straight white men can’t dance: american masculinity in film and popular culture. ifc center (greenwich village), $18 general, $15 seniors. copies of the book will also be available for purchase. >>

tues 7pm: spider man total universe with patrick a. reed + nick lowe: pop culture historian patrick a. reed launches his fully-illustrated book tracing spider-man’s comic book history from amazing fantasy #15 in 1962 to today, talking all things spidey with marvel’s spider-man editor nick lowe at your friendly neighborhood powerhouse arena (dumbo). powerhouse arena (dumbo), $5 admission includes a store gift certificate, $80 ticket option includes a copy of the book. >>

tues 7pm: this guy sucked presents: draft of shame: using sports drafting methods, podcast hosts/historians claire aubin (this guy sucked) and patrick wyman (past lives), along with commentator manny fidel (no such thing), assemble an elite team of america’s evil-est dead people and pit them against each other in a race to the bottom. caveat (les), $15 with promo code ‘skint’ (reg. $25+). >>

tues 7pm: punch puppet slam: the princess bride: a diverse group of puppet artists use a wide variety of puppet styles to tell the story of buttercup, westley, inigo, and the gang. the tank (midtown), $23. >>

tues 8pm: live band karaoke at arlene’s grocery: pick your song, grab the mic, and be a star with your very own live band (nakatomi5) backing you up at arlene’s grocery (les). bonus: online ticket purchasers are entered in raffles to win prizes like drink tickets, skip-the-line song passes, or free admission to future shows. $10 adv, $15 day-of. >>

sponsored

Ensemble photo by Fadi Kheir. Festival graphics by Saboteur Studios, UK.

Come watch The Rift, an opera in one act by renowned composer Huang Ruo and Tony Award-winning librettist David Henry Hwang. The opera tells the real-life story featured in the Oscar-winning documentary about architect Maya Lin’s iconic Vietnam Veterans Memorial in Washington, D.C.

That same evening, the Bard East/West Ensemble will perform three works written specifically for the group. The ensemble brings together a Western string quintet and seven Chinese instruments, including dizi, erhu, pipa, ruan, suona, guzheng, and sheng, alongside Chinese and Western percussionists.

The 9th annual China Now Music Festival begins at Zankel Hall at Carnegie Hall on October 2 at 7:30 p.m. This year’s theme, “Chasing Dreams,” celebrates America’s 250th anniversary by telling stories of the shared dreams, resilience, and creativity that connect us all.

Save 30% on tickets with code MUS57515 — get tickets here today!

wednesday

weds thru 10/9: 13th annual the americas film festival of new york: explore stories of historical memory, migration, identity, childhood, and music from across the americas through feature films, documentaries, shorts, filmmaker q+as, and more. various locations, free admission (except opening night). >>

weds thru fri (7:30pm): georgia gardner gray: cookie: enter a fever dream of grifters, fake tailors, and hustlers in georgia gardner gray’s site-specific performance, staged beneath the high line in the former parking lot of the meatpacking district’s last meat purveyor. free admission. >>

sponsored: weds 5-6:15pm (series ends tonight): gather round: let’s dance at manhattan west: manhattan west plaza (midtown west at 385 9th avenue) features a free weekly dance and music series in partnership with works + process featuring live bands, captivating performances, and a participatory component! this week: new york swings brings an evening of lindy hop and authentic jazz, led by choreographer gaby cook and featuring some of nyc’s top swing dancers, backed by live music from grammy-winning saxophonist josh lee and the family. >>

weds 6pm (wednesdays thru 10/21): bhangra in the plaza: watch and learn choreography that celebrates contemporary indian music and dance, right in the middle of midtown at greeley square plaza. featuring sarina jain and dancers from masala bhangra. all ages and experience levels welcome. free admission. >>

weds 6:30pm: unsinkable: poems inspired by the titanic: just steps from the titanic memorial lighthouse, the editors of unsinkable: poems inspired by the titanic come together to read from the new anthology and explore the enduring cultural resonance of the titanic. q+a with the audience and a reception will follow. south street seaport museum, free admission (rsvp). >>

weds 7pm: art21 rewind: a 25th anniversary screening: revisit the debut season of art21’s art in the twenty-first century with a screening of short artist documentaries from the series’ original 2001 season. episodes include subjects laurie anderson, mel chin, barry mcgee, shahzia sikander, and others. sva theatre (chelsea), $7. >>

weds 7pm doors (+ 10/14, 10/18): infinite good times movie club: ‘the house that carpenter built: part 1 of 3’ edition: infinite good times movie club returns with a double-feature screening of john carpenter’s big trouble in little china and they live at gowanus metal bar lucky 13 saloon. bonus: free popcorn and candy. free admission with rsvp ($5 suggested donation) >>

weds 7pm (wednesdays): baby shoes comedy: clare donaher and alex murdoch’s baby shoes comedy show delivers grown-up laughs with a fresh lineup of comedians each week. tonight’s show features grace johnson, rebecca weiser, danny palmer, and jacob chalk. black cat les, free admission. >>

weds 7:30pm (wednesdays): we have fun: a stand-up show: hosts zach sims and dan wilbur team up to bring the fun-ny to young ethel’s (south slope), with stand-up by gabe mollica (this american life), hoodo hersi (colbert), trey galyon (doug loves movies), and alex grubard (comedy central). free admission. >>

weds 8pm: charlene kaye’s 40th birthday party – king mei mei debut live show: musician and comedian charlene kaye hits 40 with the debut of her new glam-punk project, king mei mei, at littlefield (gowanus). $15. >>

weds 10pm: nyc college comedy night at ucb: four comedy teams from colleges all around the city take the upright citizen brigade stage. hosted by tess restaino and patricia lee. ucb (east village), $5. >>

thursday

thurs thru 2/8/2027: mathematics and the art of m.c. escher: discover the math behind escher’s mind-bending worlds in the first major exhibition devoted to the mathematics of his art, with more than 60 prints, drawings, original woodblocks, and other objects exploring symmetry, geometry, infinity, perspective, and the spatial logic behind his impossible scenes. free opening celebration 10/1 6:30-9pm. national museum of mathematics (flatiron), $30 general, $20 seniors/students. >>

thurs thru 10/31: archtober festival: see new york through an architect’s eyes with a month of building tours, design talks, workshops, exhibitions, film screenings, and other ways to explore the spaces that shape new york. events take place across the five boroughs with 100+ partner organizations. various prices. >>

thurs thru10/31: rooftop cinema club: catch movies under the open sky at the embassy suites skylawn rooftop in midtown, where this seasonal series screens a mix of cult favorites, classics, and newer releases. wireless headphones help block out the city noise, and drinks and classic cinema concessions are available for purchase. screenings thru october include backrooms, halloween, halloweentown, get out, ghostbusters, hocus pocus, jennifer’s body, obsession, psycho, the exorcist, the evil dead, the rocky horror picture show, weapons, and many more. $21.75+ admission (15% off for military, 10% off for students). >>

thurs 5:30pm: the king of japanese kawaii: japanese artist and harajuku kawaii pioneer sebastian masuda discusses his colorful career and the culture he helped bring to the world with fashion institute of technology professor yuniya kawamura. a book signing of kawamura’s sebastian masuda follows. fit’s katie murphy amphitheatre (chelsea), free admission. >>

thurs 6-8pm (monthly): dumbo first thursday gallery walk: 2026-27 season opener: explore dumbo’s waterfront arts scene at the first thursday gallery walk, a self-guided tour of galleries open late for receptions, artist talks, and special events. tonight’s edition includes a dozen outdoor projections and an after-party with music by dj nickodemus paired with live saxophone and percussion. free admission. >>

thurs 6:30pm: the new york i keep: an evening of obsessions, discovery, and a walk outside: hear five writers, thinkers, and deeply opinionated new yorkers make a five-minute case for the one thing they can’t stop loving about the city, then head outside together to look, notice, and maybe discover your next nyc obsession. moderated by daniel wortel-london with gabrielle bendiner-viani, moses gates, philip lopate, r.a. villanueva, and brad vogel. p+t knitwear bookstore (les), $10. >>

thurs 7:30pm: slumber party comedy show: join hosts clare donaher and shelby latterman as they split an hour of standup between campy bits, confessions, games, and more. union hall (park slope), $10 adv, $15 door. >>

thurs 9:15pm: spoons, toons, + booze: halloween after dark edition: binge watch halloween-themed cartoons from the 1940s through the 2000s on the big screen while indulging in sugary cereals and cereal-infused cocktails at secretformula’s annual screening party. hosted by michael austin and nell casey. nitehawk cinema (prospect park), $20 admission includes an all-you-can-eat cereal bar. >>

ongoing

our roundup of 40+ ongoing events: university open air, gaia, oktoberfest events, the amazing maize maze, and more. >>

item.content:encoded:
“Humorous, heartfelt, honest… a radiant celebration of love and forgiveness.” – Chicago Theatre Review

It’s 1960s Kansas, and Janice’s parents are fighting for the integration of public swimming pools — a fierce civil rights struggle that overshadows her childhood and drives a wedge between Janice and her family. It’s also thirty years later, when Janice is asked to speak at a ceremony honoring her father, forced to reckon with the scars of a past she has tried to forget. A piercing, theatrically vivid story about the personal toll of fighting for justice, and the ultimate challenge of forgiveness.

Skint readers can get $35 tickets (incl. fees) with code RIPPLESK for Tier 1 and Tier 2 tickets for Friday – Sunday performances October 23 – November 1.

GET TICKETS!

Learn more about the ripple, the wave that carried me home here.

Myrtle Avenue Negroni Week 2026
September 21–27

Bitter, Bold & Anything But Ordinary!

Negroni Week returns to Myrtle Avenue September 21–27, with 10 bars and restaurants across Fort Greene and Clinton Hill putting their own spin on the iconic cocktail. This year, bartenders venture beyond the classic trio of gin, Campari and sweet vermouth with mezcal, cherry, coffee, chocolate, rhubarb, mushrooms, orgeat…and even tomato, basil and olive oil.

Here’s what’s mixing:
• Doppelgänger – The Triangle In The Square: A smoky, ruby-red mezcal riff with Cocchi Americano, Averna and rhubarb bitters.
• The Emerson – City-Sangue Cherry Negroni: A deep-red, cherry-forward blend of Citadelle Jardin d’Été, Campari, sweet vermouth and Luxardo Sangue Morlacco.
• LaRina Pastificio & Vino – Diavolo in Me: Bright, bittersweet and slightly sour, with gin, Italian bitters, lemon, orgeat—and a little devil in it.
• Little Falcon – House Negroni: The Italian classic heads in a distinctly French direction, with a touch of French elegance.
• Lula Mae Sporting Club – Three Ways to Negroni: Choose from Classic, bright and botanical White, or smoky Mezcal.
• Neno’s – El Ahumadito Negroni: Poblano-infused mezcal gives this one a smoky Mexican spin. Try the $22 El Ahumadito Experience, pairing it with a pork belly taco.
• Osteria Brooklyn – Smoked Negroni: Gray Whale Gin, made with California-sourced botanicals, gives this riff its West Coast character.
• Putnam’s Pub – Wild Rose Negroni: Featuring Glendalough Wild Rose Gin, made with rose petals from the garden of owner Gerry Rooney’s late mother, Rose.
• Rosticceria Evelina – Five Ways to Negroni: Five inventive riffs include coffee, chocolate and the savory Negroni Pie with olive oil-washed gin, tomato-infused Campari and basil vermouth.
• Vine – Shroom Negroni: An earthy, umami-rich riff combining gin, Campari and Carpano Antica with Veda mushroom liqueur and shiitake mushroom syrup, finished with ground shiitake and an edible flower.

Drink for a cause! Each participating venue has also made a donation to Slow Food as part of Negroni Week’s global fundraising initiative.

Ten locations. Seven days. Countless ways to Negroni.

Cheers, salute, salud and sláinte…Negroni Week is back on Myrtle Avenue!

LEARN MORE HERE

friday

dolly parton appreciation day events:
► fri 9pm: dolly parton: karaoke for a cause: starr bar (bushwick), $20 admission, $2/song. >>
► fri thru 10/1: dolly parton: ifc center will always love you: the best little whorehouse in texas, steel magnolias, and 9 to 5. ifc center (greenwich village), $18 general, $15 seniors. >>

three film fests / series (various prices):
► fri-sun: 11th annual imagine this women’s international film festival: regal union square, $17.50. >>
► fri-10/1: the american cinema under george w. bush: 25th hour, jesus camp, the dark knight, war of the worlds, and more. bam rose cinemas (fort greene), $17. >>
► fri-10/12: 64th new york film festival: lincoln center’s alice tully hall, walter reade theater, and elinor bunn munroe film center. >>

sponsored: fri thru 10/25: luna stage and richard jordan productions with traverse theatre present mrs. stern wanders the prussian state library by jenny lyn bader: 1933 berlin. with martial law in effect, political activism has become a capital crime. when a young gestapo officer arrests a philosophy graduate student, her interrogation will endanger them both. inspired by the real life arrest of hannah arendt, jenny lyn bader’s thrilling and timely new play illuminates the struggle for human connection and perseverance in even the darkest of times. 59e59 theaters, use code skint to snag $29 tickets* (reg. $76-96!). >>

fri thru 10/4: the annual village trip festival: celebrating the artistic and activist history of greenwich village, the east village, and the lower east side, the eighth village trip festival returns with ‘revolutionary voices,’ 10 days of music, theater, comedy, cabaret, visual art, talks, and walking tours honoring figures including leonard bernstein, dorothy day, bob dylan, woody guthrie, eugene o’neill, and paul robeson. various prices (many events are free). >>

fri-sun (fri 7-9pm, sat 7-9pm, sun 4-6pm): dream symposium 2026: explore the strange world of dreams from the perspectives of philosophy, psychology, art, and science over three days of conversations and performances at brooklyn public library for arts + culture (fort greene). presented by the dream mapping project and the dream library foundation, the symposium includes live recordings of the podcasts this jungian life with lisa marchiano and deborah stewart, and weird studies with phil ford and j.f. martel, plus a conversation about animal dreaming with philosopher david peña-guzmán and dream researcher kelly bulkeley, followed by a performance by yuki kawahisa. free admission (rsvp). >>

sponsored: fri + sat (various times): flop house comedy club: nyc’s friendliest indie comedy club—with great comics and a cozy atmosphere—has some incredible lineups this weekend! save 50% with promo code ‘skint’ on tickets to these shows at 362 grand street in williamsburg: friday 8pm, 9:30pm, and 11pm; and the east village location is back at 201 allen st store 2 friday + saturday at 8:00pm. new: monthly member’s pass ($20) to see as many shows as you want + happy hour drinks + secret drop in announcements! >>

fri 6-9pm: bryant park square dance: bryant park sends off the summer with midtown’s biggest (only?) hoedown. the annual event features a line dancing lesson, a live band and square dancing, trick roping and lassoing lessons, a mechanical bull, and frontier-inspired crafts. country attire is encouraged, and hats and bandanas will be distributed while supplies last. food and drinks will be available for purchase. free admission. >>

fri 7pm: awkward sex… and the city storytelling show: host natalie wall and guest storytellers share personal stories about sexual mishaps, dating disasters, and other awkward encounters, finding the humor in it all. featuring guests michah eames, veronica garza, and calvin cato. friends and lovers (crown heights), $10. >>

fri 7pm: misfit variety show: comedy for weirdos, rebels, and the misunderstood: lauren logiudice’s misfit variety show assembles a rotating cast of eclectic comedy performers to celebrate the beauty of not fitting in. tonight: natasha vaynblat, dejen tesfagiorgis, siddharth raj, bob lombardi, betsy carroll, and lauren’s mom janet. eris mainstage (williamsburg), $13.70 adv, $18.99 door. >>

fri 7:30pm: friend island comedy: castaway your worries at the friend island comedy show, hosted by pals by alex murdoch and kevin mulharin. featuring performances by salma zaky, james mwaura, daniel dellanno, amelia ritthaler, cj koepp, and desmond mcdowell. fiction bar/cafe (williamsburg), $10 adv, $15 door. >>

fri 8:30pm: bitches brew comedy show: this women-produced-and-hosted comedy show conjures up big laughs in the back room of halyards (gowanus). tonight’s lineup includes ginny hogan (the new yorker), michael aaron fractor (netflix), brandi posey (lady to lady comedy), max shanker, and danielle clarke fischer. free admission (a tip jar will be passed around at the end of the show). >>

saturday

sat + sun: 21st annual brooklyn book festival: nyc’s biggest free book fest wraps with a children’s day (sat 10am-4pm), a festival day filled with 40+ talks and readings (sun 10am-6pm), and an outdoor marketplace (sun 10am-6pm). brooklyn borough hall and surrounding venues, free admission. >>

sat 6am-8pm: daybreaker – alive festival: dance, move, and connect at daybreaker’s first sunrise-to-sunset sober festival in the u.s., bringing 3,000+ people together to brooklyn bridge park’s pier 3 for a full day of music, movement, wellness, laughter, and community. all ages welcome. free admission. >>

sat 12pm: world’s biggest ‘careless whisper’ saxophone meetup: saxophonists and lovers gather in washington square park to collectively rip through george michael’s ‘careless whisper’ at the same time, led by viral social media saxophonist prazul. >>

sat 2pm: the bars we need: stories of freddy’s + prospect heights: explore how neighborhood bars and other everyday spaces help shape a community, with author gabrielle bendiner-viani sharing photos and excerpts from her book the cities we need: essential stories of everyday places, and freddy’s owner matthew kuhn telling the story of the beloved bar’s fight against demolition during the atlantic yards development. hear the stories at freddy’s current south slope location, which has been home to the bar for 15 years. a book signing will follow. free admission. >>

sat 5pm doors: bad movie night brooklyn: street fighter: pre-game for the new street fighter with bad movie night brooklyn’s screening of the 1994 cult classic starring jean-claude van damme, raul julia, ming-na wen, and kylie minogue at freddy’s bar (south slope). food and drinks will be available for purchase. free admission. >>

sat 7pm: the cultural center at st. john’s: greenpoint’s st. john’s lutheran church christents its new cultural and performing arts center with a chamber music series, continuing tonight with string quartet the rhythm method featuring noelle tannen. $20 suggested donation. >>

sat 7:30pm (monthly): flopsauce comedy show: the monthly stand-up showcase where comedians dish out their latest failures (flops) and successes (sauces) returns for more servings. tonight’s show features eric gorday, gavin rogers, george hayward, amy wieseneck, grace johnson, and amelia ritthaler. hosted by kayla kirk and emily baker. secret pour (bushwick / bed-stuy), free admission. >>

sat 9:30pm: drunk planet earth: mst3k meets animal planet meets drinking game at this participatory show that revolves around watching an animal documentary, drinking, and the audience trying to stump the hosts with animal trivia. hosted by brian morabito and stephen buckley. caveat (les), free admission. >>

sponsored: sat 10:30pm: be my baby! a motown soul party!: dj little sally is comin’ atcha with the fourth edition of be my baby! a motown soul party! from martha reeves and the vandellas to the supremes, tammi terrell to the shirelles, and every 60’s song to ever make your heart skip a beat, dj little sally is bringing all the motown, girl groups, and funky grooves so hot you’ll feel ’em in your soul. ps: don’t forget to limber up for the midnight limbo rock competition! winner gets $50 in cash! alphaville (bushwick), $13.06 adv, $15 day of/door. >>

sunday

sun 1-4:30pm: walt whitman initiative’s 23rd annual ‘song of myself’ marathon : join the annual marathon reading of whitman’s celebrated poem ‘song of myself,’ with all 52 sections performed aboard the historic tall ship wavertree at south street seaport. note: in case of rain, the event will be held across the street at the walt whitman initiative tane poetry library. free admission. >>

sun 3pm: jim henson’s birthday costume contest: dress as your favorite muppet, puppeteer, or your own original character for a costume contest celebrating the man behind kermit, with prizes awarded by a panel of judges including special guest kate micucci. enter solo or with a group, or come cheer on the costumed chaos. museum of the moving image’s kaufman courtyard (astoria), free admission. >>

sun 6pm + 8:30pm: stand up comedy special taping: mindy raf’s a (very) nervous system: mindy raf comes to littlefield (gowanus) with a comedy hour that questions what is considered ‘normal’ while focusing on the modern spectrum of relationships, identity, and what it’s like being in a very nervous system. $18.71 with promo code ‘skintspecial’ (reg. $24.36). >>

monday

mon 6:30pm doors: movies at the palace: season of courage: sunset boulevard: united palace’s movies at the palace screening series returns with a lineup celebrating bold heroes, big dreams, and unforgettable stories. the season continues with billy wilder’s sunset boulevard (1950), with a pre-show performance by bilingual broadway collective. united palace (washington heights), $10. >>

mon 7pm: three-day champion: a comedic storytelling podcast wrapped inside a game show where comedian contestants are asked, ‘if you were a three-day champion on a game show, what three stories about yourself would you choose to tell?’ hosted by christine walters with jenny zigrino, cipha sounds, and roy wood jr. caveat (les), $19.93 with promo code ‘cechamp’ (reg. $24.93). >>

mon 7pm: the accessible comedy show: this inclusive stand-up show brings together deaf and hearing comedians and audiences, with every performance interpreted in both asl and voice. deaf comics sign their sets with voice interpretation, while hearing comics perform alongside asl interpreters, bridging two communities over comedy. ucb (east village), $15. >>

mon 7pm: broadway nights off: broadway stars betsy wolfe (+ juliet, death becomes her, little shop of horrors) and adam kantor (rent, fiddler on the roof) share the stage for an evening of musical theater favorites with a waterfront view at downtown’s robert f. wagner park. free admission. >>

mon 8pm: the astigmatism comedy show: ‘black women with poor vision but excellent taste’ present a stand-up show with a chance to win a signed book of the month. hosted by kristal adams, alexis bradby, katrina davis, and isabelle pierre at book club bar (east village), with q+a featuring guest author daniella toosie-watson (what we do with god). $15 admission includes $8 off any drink at the bar. >>

mon 9:30pm: 6 degrees of cats (the animal, not the musical) live!: join 6 degrees of cats podcast host amanda b. for a night of games, feline facts, laughs, trivia, and prizes featuring comedian marina franklin (single black female), burlesque producer and podcast host gemma smith (catbaret, tails + tassels), and more. caveat (les), unlock $15 tickets with code ‘skint’ (reg. $24-25). >>
